name: Historic Centre of Évora
description: Évora is a walled town in Portugal's sun-baked Alentejo region, where a Roman temple still stands among lanes of whitewashed houses. The city flourished in the 15th century as a home of Portuguese kings, and many of its houses are decked with blue-and-white azulejo tiles and wrought-iron balconies from the 16th to 18th centuries. Its monuments even shaped Portuguese architecture in Brazil.
